newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria PM vows to fight rebels, pledges free vote.
newsitem.headline: Algeria PM vows to fight rebels, pledges free vote.

text.p: Algerian Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, presenting his government's programme before the National Assembly, said on Saturday the state was determined to defeat Moslem guerrillas and promised fair local elections in October.
Ouyahia said government forces, backed by ever-increasing numbers of Algerians opposed to Moslem militants, had the upper hand against the guerrillas who have been fighting the government since 1992.

"Terrorism, which has suffered a defeat at the hands of the nationalist forces, was the result of a wide-ranging conspiracy against the nation," he told the 380-member assembly in a speech broadcast on state television.
Algerian officials usually call Moslem rebels "terrorists" and "criminals".

Some 700 civilians have been killed in a series of massacres and attacks blamed by the authorities on Moslem rebels June 5, when Algeria held a general election which voters and officials had hoped would help usher in peace and stability.
About 300 rebels were reported killed in a two-week government offensive in July.

In the latest reported violence, Algerian newspapers said on Saturday that suspected Moslem guerrillas had killed 14 people by cutting their throats or heads in four attacks across the country this week.
"Algeria is determined to fight the barbaric and criminal terrorism phenomenon which is targeting the Algerian people without discrimination," Ouyahia said.
"Awareness and collective mobilisation against terrorism are imperative," he said.

Ouyahia's three-party coalition cabinet, formed after the June election, is dominated by President Liamine Zeroual's supporters and includes seven moderate Islamists and seven members of the former ruling National Liberation Front.
In the October election voters will choose officials to run Algeria's 48 cities and 1,500 towns and villages.
"Thanks to dialogue and the conditions met by the government, the election on October 23 will take place in an atmosphere of freedoom and transparency," Ouyahia said.
Most of the local authorities are run by government officials appointed after elected representatives from the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) were sacked for allegedly backing rebels.
Those elected in the October vote will also choose two-thirds of the of a new upper house, the 144-member Council of the Nation.
Zeroual will appoint the other third of the council which with the National Assembly forms the parliament.
About 60,000 people have been killed in the North African country since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a huge lead.
